blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: In this paper, we study the higher Hochschild chain[^1] complex $CH^{{\scriptstyle\bullet}}_{X_\bullet}(A)$, functorially assigned to a simplicial set $X_\bullet$ (or a topological space), and a commutative differential graded algebra (CDGA) $A$, from an axiomatic point of view. Recently, motivated by topological quantum field theories, several concepts integrating (higher) categories of spaces or manifolds with those of algebras of different types have arisen. We also study the relationship between higher Hochschild chains, factorization algebras [@CG; @Co], topological chiral homology [@L-TF

blocks.title: Preliminary definitions and notation
blocks.content:
In this section we recall some standard definitions and constructions.

**Conventions:**

1.  We fix a ground field $k$ of characteristic zero. The $(\infty,1)$-category of differential graded $k$-modules (*i.e.* complexes) will be denoted $k\textit{-}Mod_\infty$.

2.  The (naïve) categories of simplicial sets and of commutative differential graded algebras will be respectively denoted by $sSet$ and $CDGA$. The category of commutative graded algebra will be denoted $CGA$. Unless otherwise stated, all algebras will be assumed to be *unital*.

[]{#S:Delta label="S:Delta"} Denote by $\Delta$ the category whose objects are the ordered sets $[k]=\{0,1,\dots,k\}$, and morphisms $f:[k]\to [l]$ are non-decreasing maps $f(i)\geq f(j)$ for $i>j$. blocks.content: []{#S:CDGA label="S:CDGA"} We let $CDGA$ be the category of commutative differential graded algebras (over the characteristic zero field $k$). We do not assume the underlying chain complexes of our algebras to be bounded since in practice, it happens that one has to consider the Hochschild chains of de Rham forms on a space, which is generally $\mathbb Z$-graded. blocks.title: Naive axiomatic approach to higher Hochschild homology
blocks.content:
[]{#S:NaiveHH label="S:NaiveHH"}

We first recall the standard construction of chain complexes computing higher Hochschild homology (also called Hochschild homology over spaces) following [@P; @GTZ]. The higher Hochschild complex is a functor $CH: sSet \times CDGA \to CDGA$. This functor is defined as follows: the tensor products $A\otimes B$ of two CDGAs has an natural structure of CDGA(in other words, $CDGA$ has a symmetric monoidal structure canonically induced by the underlying tensor product of chain complexes). Locally constant factorization algebras and En-algebras

[]{#S:ReviewTCH label="S:ReviewTCH"}

Let $A$ be an $E_n$-algebra and $M$ a manifold of dimension $m$ which is *(stably) $n$-framed*, that is a manifold of dimension $m$ equipped with a framing of $M\times D^{n-m}$. The **topological chiral homology** of $M$ with coefficients in $A$ was defined in [@L-TFT; @L-VI] and [@Francis] and will be denoted $\int_{M} A$. Note that the above definition *does* depend on the framing in general, even though it is not explicit in the notation[^1]. Further $\int_M A$ is an $E_{n-m}$-algebra in general, see [@L-TFT; @L-VI].
